topic_en: Rust struct + impl: adding methods to your data

xhs.title: Rust 没有 class，方法写哪？
xhs.body:
第 10 课：struct + impl
struct 放数据，impl 放方法
&self 只读借用，&mut self 能改字段，self 直接拿走所有权
不带 self 的是关联函数，比如 Rect::new，用 :: 调用
有 self 用点调用：r.area()
考考你：impl 里写 fn inc(&self) { self.n += 1; } 能编译吗？ 评论区告诉我～

tiktok.body: Rust has no classes. So where do methods go? struct holds the data, impl holds the methods. Quick quiz: fn inc(&self) { self.n += 1; }  Does it compile? Comment your answer.

linkedin.title: Rust has no classes. Here is where methods go.
linkedin.body:
A struct holds the data; an impl block holds the methods.
The first parameter says what a method does with the value: &self reads it, &mut self modifies it, self takes ownership.
A function with no self is an associated function, like Rect::new, called with ::.
Methods are called with a dot: r.area().
Quick quiz: inside impl Counter, fn inc(&self) { self.n += 1; }  Does it compile? Answer in the comments.

quiz.q_zh: impl Counter { fn inc(&self) { self.n += 1; } } 能编译吗？
quiz.q_en: impl Counter { fn inc(&self) { self.n += 1; } }  Does it compile?
quiz.answer_zh: 答案：不能。&self 是只读借用，不能改字段。要改就写 fn inc(&mut self)。
quiz.answer_en: Answer: no. &self is a read-only borrow, so you can't change a field through it. Use fn inc(&mut self) instead.
